test_title: SSC CPO 2023 Official Paper-II (Held On: 08 Jan, 2024)
subject: general
question:
Parts of the given sentence have been given as options. One of them contains a grammatical error. Select the option that has the error.

The captain along with all the sailors were warmly welcomed back home by the town people.

options.text: along with all the sailors were

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the second part of the given sentence, the plural form of the verb 'were' is incorrect.
 
• In the given sentence, one **subject 'captain'** is **singular** and the other **subject 'sailors'** is **plural**.
 
• If **one subject is singular and the other is plural** and the words are **connected by** the words "not/but, not, **or, nor, neither/nor, either/or, not only/but also, etc**.", use the **verb form of the subject** (here, **captain**) that is **nearest or closest to the verb**.
 
 
• **Example:** ***Neither** the **lion** **nor** the **elephants have** escaped from the zoo*.
 
 
 
• Therefore, the singular form of the verb 'was' should be used in place of the plural form 'were'.

Hence, the correct statement is** ** '*The captain along with all the sailors **was warmly welcomed** back home by the town people*.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• If the **subjects are both singular** and are **connected by** the words "not/but, not, or, nor, neither/nor, either/or, not only/but also, etc." the **verb is singular**.

 
 
• **Example:** ***Either Sita or Geeta is** to blame for the accident*.
 
 
 
• If the **subjects are both plurals** and are **connected by** the words "not/but, not, or, nor, neither/nor, either/or, not only/but also, etc." the **verb is plural**.
 
 
• Example: ***Not only dogs but also cats are** available at the shelter*.
